pr_title: fix(compiler): support i18n interpolated only attribute bindings
pr_body:
While fully dynamic bound properties (and attributes) cannot be marked for localization, properties that only contain interpolation can.

This commit ensure that attribute bindings that only contain interpolation can also be marked for localization.

Closes #43260

@petebacondarwin I've performed the necessary investigation and found the origin of the problem. The template that can be used for repro: ```
``` It's important to have an attribute that doesn't directly translate to a property. The underlying problem is that the `i18nAttributes` instruction that we generate actually sets a property on an element, not an attribute (taking an advantage that attribute translations were not supported by the compiler), see: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/a91fe6db8ce76f8ccf09a364f16b828f59322025/packages/core/src/render3/i18n/i18n_apply.ts#L279-L296 We end up calling `elementPropertyInternal`. It worked for the test case that we had, since: ``` const div = document.createElement('div'); div.title = 'abc'; div.getAttribute('title'); // outputs 'abc' ``` But for attributes like `aria-label`, that would not work (we'd just set a property, which would actually be incorrect). It looks like the mentioned code in the `i18n_apply.ts` should have a clear indication when we should set an attribute vs a property for an element (in addition to the current `if` check that we have there). We might consider introducing 2 instructions: `i18nAttributes` and `i18nProperties`, which would use different OpCodes, so that the code in the `i18n_apply.ts` can differentiate between attributes and properties.

FYI we also have a code that maps attribute names that don't correspond to their element property names:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/core/src/render3/instructions/shared.ts#L1004

So we can potentially consider expanding the logic in the `i18n_apply.ts` (or the `shared.ts`) to have some extra mapping logic, but it would be either too heavy from code size perspective (if we just put 1:1 mapping for ARIA and other attributes) or too slow (if we try to apply some transform to an attribute name).

Should we reopen the original issue then (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/43260)? 
It currently looks like it's resolved, which is misleading (I actually ended up running through the changelog, and then looking at the PRs again, just to learn the fix has been reverted)

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler, localize ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description i18n doesn't produce the output I'd expect when used on an `attr.attr-name` attribute. My hope here is to be able to translate interpolated aria attributes, e.g.: `` -- which I am trying to use because Angular rejects an interpolated `aria-label` without the `attr.`. My example here uses `title` instead of `aria-label` just so I can provide more "working" variations. 1. Create a new project with the CLI and `ng add @angular/localize`. 2. Put the following in app.component.html ```html

``` 3. Run `npm start` and visit in a browser. I see the following rendered markup: ```html

 ``` The `title` attribute is misnamed `attr.title` in case 3 and is omitted in case 4. I would expect the following instead: ```html

case 1

case 2

case 4

 ``` v11.2.14 with Ivy enabled gives the same output as v12. With Ivy disabled, case 4 has a `title` attribute as expected. Case 3 still has `attr.title` in the output either way. (Case 3 is output as a literal `attr.title` even without i18n; am I misunderstanding how `attr.` is supposed to work, or is that wrong as well?) 4. Run `ng extract-i18n` In the resulting messages.xlf file, case 4 is missing. I tried this with Angular v11.2.14 and if ivy is disabled, it gives the expected result (all four cases present); if ivy is enabled, case 4 is missing. v12 and v11 with Ivy enabled: ```xml case 1 src/app/app.component.html 1 case src/app/app.component.html 2 case 3 src/app/app.component.html 3 ``` v11 with Ivy disabled: ```xml case 1 src/app/app.component.html 1 case src/app/app.component.html 2 case 3 src/app/app.component.html 3 case src/app/app.component.html 4 ``` --- And of course if it worked up to this point, I'd try including translations for case 3/4 and check that they were replaced like other attributes with i18n. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-tp6jnh?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html ### Please provide the exception or error you saw _No response_ ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in ```true Angular: 12.2.2 default packages (from ng new) + @angular/localize ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

Here is another reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-ebm42l?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html ```html

case 1

case 2

case 3

case 4

case 5

case 6

aria 1

aria 3

aria 4

aria 5

aria 6

``` Only three i18n messages are generated: ```ts i18n_0 = $localize `:@@case1:case 1`; i18n_2 = $localize `:@@case2:case ${{ '{' }}"\uFFFD0\uFFFD"}:INTERPOLATION:`; i18n_4 = $localize `:@@aria1:aria 1`; ``` * `case 1` and `aria 1` are expected and correct: the system correctly generates i18n messages for static attributes that are marked with `i18n-...`. * `case 2` is correct and expected: the system is able to generate an i18n message for an interpolated property (not attribute). This only works because the DOM element has a `title` property as well as a `title` attribute - and the two are mapped to each other by the DOM. Unfortunately, as mentioned in this issue, it is not possible to use this approach for ARIA attributes since they do not have an equivalent DOM property. * `case 3` and `aria 3` are correct and expected: the i18n message extraction is not able to process property bindings of the form: `[prop]="expression"`. By the way, this is the correct usage of `attr....` to bind any expression to an attribute - as documented in https://angular.io/guide/attribute-binding#binding-aria-attributes So finally we come to cases 4, 5 and 6. * 4 and 6 set the `title`/`aria-label` correctly, but do not generate an i18n message * 5 does neither! I think that case 4 is actually the usage that we want to support. When matching `i18n-` markers to attributes we should ignore the `attr.` prefix from the attribute name. So I think that is the bug that needs to be fixed. Probably around this bit of code: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/4c00e92023c526af5e09c684c78ebbf630eb150b/packages/compiler/src/render3/view/i18n/meta.ts#L92-L105

@strout thanks for creating a ticket and describing the issue.

@petebacondarwin thanks for the investigation! The current logic in inline with ViewEngine extraction mechanisms (in VE the `attr.xyz` is not extracted), but since VE is now deprecated (and people would not be switching between Ivy/VE anymore), we can extend Ivy to take care of more scenarios. I think scenario 4 and 5 are good candidates. My only concern regarding scenario 4 (`attr.aria-label="aria {{4}}" i18n-aria-label="@@aria4"`) is that it might not be straightforward for users since the existing mental model is that you just prefix whatever you want to translate with `i18n-`, so I'm leaning towards `i18n-attr.xyz` as a marker. However we can also consider supporting both `i18n-attr.xyz` and `i18n-xyz`. What do you think?

> However we can also consider supporting both i18n-attr.xyz and i18n-xyz. What do you think?

I was just thinking about this as well, and I think that is perfectly feasible.
